messages:
Alex (eng-infra): Heads-up — seeing odd behaviour in eu-west1 tonight: fractional-GPU pods (MIG/time-slice) Pending for ~45s even after the node reports Ready. Not seeing this on full-GPU nodepools. Anyone else?
Priya (eng-sre): @Alex :eyes: Can you paste a `kubectl describe pod` and node events? Are we hitting IP/ENI limits or kubelet device-plugin timeouts?
Alex (eng-infra): Quick paste:
```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  50s   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ...
  Normal  Pulling    49s   kubelet            Pulling image "..."
  Normal  Pulled     48s   kubelet            Successfully pulled image
  Warning Failed     45s   kubelet            failed to allocate gpu device: device plugin not ready
  Normal  Started    4s    kubelet            Started container
```
Node: `Ready` at -6s but kubelet logs show device plugin re-register / init taking ~30s.
Mateo (eng-runtime): That sounds like the NVidia plugin / MIG driver warmup. With time-sliced drivers we see kernel module init and container runtime handshake delays. We added a recent change to `device-plugin` that retries more but still waits for MIG profile probing.
Jing (eng-ml): This matches some eval runs we saw: short lived bursty traffic loses first 1-2 tokens throughput because the MIG context isn't warmed. Might explain the 45s hang when pods try to start immediately after scale-up.
Sam (eng-oncall): Region detail: only happening in eu-west1-c AZ, not in other AZs. Could be a node image variation or kernel ABI mismatch. I can roll one node to run diagnostics if we want to repro.
Priya (eng-sre): Also check cluster-autoscaler config. If CA adds node then immediately schedules many pods, the device-plugin can become a hot spot. Consider adding a `scale_up_unneeded_time` / `cooldown` to avoid packing too many fractional-GPU pods at once.
Alex (eng-infra): Current autoscaler snippet:
```
apiVersion: cluster.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 10m
  scaleUpDelay: 0s
  maxNodesTotal: 200
```
I think `scaleUpDelay` of 0s is too aggressive for fractional pools.
Mateo (eng-runtime): Two concrete mitigations: 1) keep a small warm pool of 1-2 fractional nodes (tainted, tolerated by low-priority warmup pods) so device-plugin is live; 2) tune CA to use `expander: least-waste` and add a 30-60s `scaleUpDelay` for this nodepool. The warm pool costs a bit but saves user latency.
Jing (eng-ml): From perf side, we also saw less variance if we pin the first job to a whole-GPU node for the warmup, then migrate subsequent small jobs to fractional pool. Not ideal but works for critical low-latency paths.
Sam (eng-oncall): I ran `journalctl -u kubelet` on the node; found repeated device-plugin reconnects. Also found `ENI allocation` near limit on that AZ's subnet which could block new Node IP allocation. Not sure if that was a coincidence.
Priya (eng-sre): Good call — ENI/IPv4 exhaustion can make nodes Ready but scheduling fail in weird ways. Check `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` / GCP equivalent for free IPs. For now, can we pin fractional pools to smaller subnets?
Alex (eng-infra): Proposal: create a dedicated fractional-gpu nodepool with:
- 2 min nodes (warm pool)
- max 30 nodes
- `scaleUpDelay: 45s` for this pool
- CA expander set to `least-waste` for fractional pool only
- taint `fractional-warm=true:NoSchedule` and run a warmup DaemonSet that loads GPU drivers + a short loop warp to keep MIG contexts alive
Pros: lower P99 startup latency. Cons: extra baseline cost.
Mateo (eng-runtime): Implementation note: warmup DaemonSet should use `hostPID: true`? Better to keep it in container namespace but run an init script that calls `nvidia-smi -L` and a small loop: `for i in 1..100; do ./warmup_bin; sleep 10; done` so MIG contexts stay cached.
Jing (eng-ml): We should also add a metric `gpu_warmup_failures_total` + `scale_up_wait_seconds` and alert when P95 startup > 20s. That will help quantify cost vs benefit.
Priya (eng-sre): Quick action items:
- Sam: check AZ IP capacity + subnet fragmentation in eu-west1-c (ETA: 1h)
- Mateo: prototype warmup DaemonSet and test driver re-register times on canary nodes (ETA: 2d)
- Alex: create fractional nodepool CA config PR with `scaleUpDelay: 45s` and expander change (ETA: 1d)
- Jing: add perf metric + dashboard for startup latency (ETA: 3d)
Sam (eng-oncall): On it — will also run a node image diff between eu-west1-c and other AZs.
Alex (eng-infra): One more thought — for spot/preemptible nodes we should be conservative: keep warm-pool in on-demand and let CA burst spots for additional capacity. Preemptions kill warm contexts.
Mateo (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also consider making device-plugin startup idempotent/parallel so large spikes don't serialize plugin init. I'll look at the plugin backlog queue.
deploy-bot: Deployed `gpu-plugin:v2.3.1` to canary nodes at 1980004400 :shipit:
Alex (eng-infra): Great — let's sync tomorrow after the canary results. If warm-pool + `scaleUpDelay` reduces P95 from ~45s to <10s then we roll to prod. Thanks team :thumbsup:
